summary: A very common surface fungus on squash, pumpkin and other cucurbits. Leaves die early, so fruit are smaller, sunburnt and store poorly.
symptoms: White, powdery spots on both leaf surfaces, starting on older leaves
Spots merge until the whole leaf is white
Leaves yellow, brown and die early
key_sign: White, flour-like powder on leaves that wipes off with a finger.
favourable_conditions: Warm days, dense plantings and shade; it does not need rain or leaf wetness to infect.
spread: Spores spread long distances by wind.

today: Remove the worst-affected older leaves to slow spread
this_week: Start a fungicide programme registered for cucurbit powdery mildew as soon as the first spots appear
Space or thin plants for airflow and sunlight
next_two_weeks: Repeat at label intervals; alternate fungicide groups to prevent resistance
Keep checking the undersides of older leaves

chemical: Sulfur, or targeted fungicides labelled for cucurbit powdery mildew; rotate FRAC groups because resistance develops quickly
organic: Sulfur (not in hot weather), potassium bicarbonate, horticultural oils, or Bacillus-based biofungicides
cultural: Plant in full sun with good spacing
